subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What do the letters CPU stand for?
questions.explain: The CPU (Central Processing Unit) is the component that processes instructions and data in a computer.

questions.q: In the von Neumann architecture, what is held in memory alongside the data?
questions.explain: A key feature of the von Neumann model is that program instructions and data share the same memory (the stored-program concept).

questions.q: What is the main function of the Arithmetic and Logic Unit (ALU)?
options: To carry out arithmetic and logical operations
To store the operating system permanently
To connect the computer to a network
To convert analogue signals to sound
questions.explain: The ALU performs calculations (such as addition) and logical comparisons within the CPU.

questions.q: What does the Memory Address Register (MAR) hold?
options: The address of the memory location to be accessed
The actual data read from memory
The next instruction to be decoded
questions.explain: The MAR stores the address of the memory location that is about to be read from or written to.

questions.q: What does the Memory Data Register (MDR) hold?
options: The data or instruction being transferred to or from memory
The address of the next instruction
The clock speed of the processor
questions.explain: The MDR temporarily stores the data or instruction that is being moved between the CPU and memory.

questions.q: Which register holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched?
questions.explain: The Program Counter stores the address of the next instruction and is incremented during the fetch stage.

questions.q: A processor's clock speed is increased from 2 GHz to 4 GHz. What is the most likely effect?
options: More fetch-execute cycles are carried out each second, so processing is generally faster
The amount of RAM is automatically doubled
Data is permanently deleted from cache
questions.explain: A higher clock speed means more instruction cycles per second, so the CPU can generally process instructions more quickly.

questions.q: Why does a CPU use cache memory?
options: To store frequently used instructions and data close to the CPU for faster access
To provide permanent storage for user files
To connect the computer to the internet
To display graphics on the monitor
questions.explain: Cache is small, fast memory that holds frequently used data, reducing the time the CPU waits to fetch from slower RAM.

questions.q: What are the three stages of the machine (fetch-execute) cycle, in order?
questions.explain: During each cycle an instruction is fetched from memory, decoded, and then executed by the CPU.

questions.q: Which of the following is an input device?
questions.explain: A barcode reader sends data into the computer, so it is an input device; the others are output devices.

questions.q: A smartphone touch screen is best described as which type of device?
options: Both an input and an output device
questions.explain: A touch screen displays output and also detects touch as input, so it performs both roles.

questions.q: A home user wants to print a small number of high-quality colour photographs. Which printer is most suitable?
questions.explain: Inkjet printers produce high-quality colour images and are well suited to low-volume photo printing at home.

questions.q: What is the purpose of an actuator in a control system?
options: To convert electrical signals into physical movement or action
To read data from a barcode
To display images on a screen
questions.explain: An actuator is an output component that turns signals from the processor into movement, such as opening a valve or turning a motor.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of magnetic storage?
questions.explain: A hard disk drive stores data magnetically on spinning platters, making it magnetic storage.

questions.q: Which statement about a solid-state drive (SSD) is correct?
options: It stores data using flash memory and has no moving parts
It uses a laser to read pits and lands
It stores data on magnetic tape
It relies on spinning platters and read/write heads
questions.explain: SSDs use solid-state flash memory, so they contain no moving mechanical parts.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of optical storage?
questions.explain: Optical storage such as CDs, DVDs and Blu-ray discs is read and written using a laser.

questions.q: Taking 1 GB as 1024 MB, how many 4 MB photographs can be stored on a 1 GB memory card?
questions.explain: 1024 MB divided by 4 MB per photo gives 256 photographs.

questions.q: What is a key difference between RAM and ROM?
options: RAM is volatile and loses its contents when power is off, whereas ROM is non-volatile
RAM is non-volatile whereas ROM is volatile
Both RAM and ROM lose their contents when switched off
Neither RAM nor ROM can be read by the CPU
questions.explain: RAM is volatile primary storage, while ROM retains its contents without power and is non-volatile.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a router in a network?
options: To forward data packets between different networks, such as a home network and the internet
To convert sound into an electrical signal
To display web pages on the screen
questions.explain: A router directs data packets between networks, for example connecting a local network to the internet.

questions.q: Why does a computer need a network interface card (NIC)?
options: To allow it to connect to a network and give it a unique MAC address
To increase the amount of RAM available
To speed up the processor's clock
questions.explain: A NIC provides the hardware and a unique MAC address that let a device connect to and communicate on a network.
